question: The national animal of Nepal is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**cow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The cow is officially recognized as the **national animal of Nepal**.
 
• In Nepal, the cow holds a sacred status, particularly in **Hindu culture**, where it is revered as a symbol of prosperity and motherhood.
 
• The cow was declared the national animal of Nepal in **2015** after the promulgation of the new constitution.
 
• The constitution of Nepal prohibits the **slaughter of cows**, emphasizing its cultural and religious importance.
 
• The cow is deeply integrated into Nepalese traditions and is celebrated during the festival of **Tihar**, where it is worshipped as part of the festivities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cultural Significance of Cows in Hinduism:**

 
 
• Cows are considered sacred in Hinduism and are often referred to as "Gau Mata" (Mother Cow).
 
• They are associated with various deities, particularly Lord Krishna and Goddess Lakshmi.
 
• The cow is a symbol of **non-violence** and nurturing, representing wealth and abundance.
 
 
 
• **Nepal's Constitution and Cow Protection:**
 
 
• Nepal's constitution explicitly prohibits the slaughter of cows, making it a punishable offense.
 
• This legal protection aligns with the religious sentiments of the majority Hindu population.
 
 
 
• **Other National Symbols of Nepal:**
 
 
• National bird: Himalayan Monal (Danphe).
 
• National flower: Rhododendron (Lali Gurans).
 
• National flag: The unique double-triangle flag of Nepal.
 
 
 
• **Tihar Festival:**
 
 
• Tihar is a major Hindu festival celebrated in Nepal, also known as the festival of lights.
 
• One of the days is dedicated to cow worship, where cows are adorned with garlands and offered food.
